messages:
alexw: Hi all — Alex here, just joined the runtime team. Trying to build the runtime from source on my dev box and hitting a linker error. Can someone point me to the usual checklist?

alexw: Environment: Ubuntu 22.04 VM (x86_64), NVIDIA driver 525.60, CUDA toolkit installed under /usr/local/cuda-12.0, nvcc reports 12.0. CMake run seemed fine but make fails with: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/redwood-runtime.dir/src/main.o: in function `main':
main.cpp:(.text+0x123): undefined reference to `cuInit'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

alexw: I have CUDA_HOME set to /usr/local/cuda, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /usr/local/cuda/lib64.

paige: welcome! :wave: quick checks: `nvidia-smi` shows the driver is loaded? also `nvcc --version` output please.

alexw: nvidia-smi works and shows driver 525.60.0, GPUs OK. nvcc --version prints CUDA 12.0.

oliver: undefined reference to cuInit usually means the linker didn't pick up cudart (libcudart.so). Are you using the system link dirs or static link? Check the final link command in the build output (look for -lcudart or -L flags).

alexw: Good point — the cmake link line doesn't have -lcudart. CMakeLists uses find_package(CUDA) and then links ${CUDA_LIBRARIES}. Seems empty.

paige: we recently switched to CMake's CUDA language and use CMAKE_CUDA_RUNTIME_LIBRARY. If your cmake cached old vars it may not set libcudart. Try `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` from a clean build dir. Also run `cmake --build build --target link-plugins VERBOSE=1` to inspect link flags.

infra-bot: FYI: there is an open infra note about mismatched CUDA symlink names on some VMs. If /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.0 is missing the canonical path check will fail.

samir: if you want a fast workaround, use our dev docker image: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/dev-runtime:cuda12 /bin/bash` and build there — it has the right toolchain.

alexw: I tried the docker image and the linker step passes there, thanks. But then I hit a ptxas fatal during JIT compile of kernels: 
```
ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not recognized for option '--gpu-name'
```

oliver: that usually means the toolkit's ptxas doesn't recognize the requested arch. Check CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES or the CUDA_ARCH flags. What GPU model do you have?

alexw: It's an RTX A6000 (compute capability 8.0). I saw sm_80 and sm_86 bits in different places — maybe some CMake cache set sm_86.

ryan: set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80` (or a list like "80;86" if you support both). Also ensure your ptxas and nvcc are the same toolkit version as the libcuda driver. Mismatches can produce weird ptxas errors.

paige: one more gotcha — on some distros the system GCC is too new for nvcc and produces ABI mismatches. If you hit C++ symbol errors later, try building with Ubuntu's gcc-9 toolchain or use the docker image which pins GCC.

alexw: OK I'll try a clean build with cmake + explicit CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80 and confirm. Thanks for the pointers!

alexw: Update — clean build with `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80` fixed the ptxas error and linking now works locally. Using docker image still recommended for first-day setup. Opening a tiny onboarding doc PR with the common fixes. :+1:

paige: amazing, welcome aboard and great debugging writeup. Ping if you want a quick pairing to finalize the PR.

samir: also adding a short note to infra tickets about the symlink issue.

alexw: thanks everyone :heart:
